articles.headline: AI price gouging might have indirectly hit HP's notebook output as supplier reportedly halted shipment
keyFacts: Quanta Computer reportedly halted HP notebook production for about a week in September after contract price negotiations stalled, according to media reports.
The dispute centered on rising costs for parts like batteries and circuit boards amid Quanta's expanding AI server business, reports indicated.
Production resumed after senior HP executives met with Quanta in Taiwan and accepted a renegotiated cost adjustment.
body: - Quanta reportedly halted HP notebook production for about a week after price talks stalled
- The dispute centered around ODM-bought parts like PCBs, batteries and power chips, while HP already assumes most memory CPU and GPU costs directly
- Shipments were resumed once HP executives renegotiated a hike

Quanta Computer, the Taiwanese contract manufacturer that builds a large share of HP's laptops, reportedly stopped producing HP notebooks for about a week in September 2026 after the two companies failed to agree on prices.
DigiTimes reports that Quanta cut off supply to press HP into paying more, drawing on a server business that has grown to dwarf its laptop operation.

A fuller account comes from Taiwan People News, which cites supply chain sources saying Quanta co-founder and vice chairman C.C. Leung personally ordered the halt once September negotiations stalled with production resuming only after senior HP executives stepped in with a cost adjustment that Quanta accepted.
AI servers changed the math as buyers continue to pay the price

The story does lack official confirmation, as Quanta told the Taiwan People News that it "does not respond regarding individual customers," and German outlet heise reported that HP has not commented on the issue to date.

Despite this, something that would have been unimaginable only a few years ago, is now entirely plausible, even if one cant find direct evidence for it. The historical improbability has a reason: contract manufacturers rely on scale to spread their fixed costs, and a large order ties up purchasing, capacity and staffing, so even unattractive pricing rarely leads an ODM to switch off a major account.

Heise, which describes HP as Quanta's largest notebook customer, states that HP had refused to share rising production costs and insisted on previously agreed prices, unlike other PC brands, and that HP sent supply chain executives to Taiwan to deal with Leung directly. What it had to give up to get shipments going again has not been make public even as Digitimes states it forced HP to raise prices.

The two companies have some legal history here that seems prudent to highlight: HP won a $438.7 million optical drive price-fixing judgment against Quanta's subsidiary Quanta Storage before settling confidentially in June 2020.

It is important to provide context: most of the more expensive components: GPUs, CPUs and RAM are all sourced directly by HP and it has already pushed price increases back to consumers. The parts Quanta buys on its own account are a different list: printed circuit boards, passive components, lithium batteries, power management chips and Wi-Fi chips, all of which have faced price pressure lately.

When those rise, the cost lands on Quanta unless the contract is reopened or renegotiated, and swapping in cheaper parts brings its own bill for redesign, certification and one-time engineering fees. Quanta seems to be extremely well-fed to want to bother with shouldering additional costs in an industry that is dwarfed by data center servers that make up as much as 80% of its revenue thanks to a surge in AI demand.

There is however a lack of corroborating evidence that this happened: Quanta does not break out shipments by customer, but its totals show no obvious September hole. The company shipped 4.2 million notebooks in September, up 61.5% from August and down 8.7% from a year earlier, according to the same Anue report.

There are reasons a halt might not show up in those totals. Quanta also builds laptops for Apple, including the MacBook Neo, and other customers' volumes could cover an HP gap relatively with ease. Alternatively a one-week production stop also need not become a one-week shipment gap if finished inventory was on hand or output was caught up before the month closed.

Irrespective of whatever happened and whatever was potentially agreed to in Taiwan, the bill flows downstream and consumers are ultimately asked to pay the price. For two decades, PC brands could make their contract manufacturers eat cost increases because those manufacturers had few better places to put their factories.

Quanta now has one if the account holds and other ODMs with fast-growing server businesses will have noticed that a week without HP did not sink Quanta. HP's competitors will have noticed the same too and it might factor into their own negotiations or renegotiations in the future even customers continue pony an increasingly large bill.

articles.headline: 'Common Side Effects' Officially Break Their Silence on Season 2 Plans
keyFacts: Co-creators Joe Bennett and Steve Hely announced that Common Side Effects season 2 will premiere January 24 on Adult Swim.
Season 2 introduces a new villain named Thomas and explores shared hallucinations caused by the Blue Angel mushroom.
The creators expanded the show's animation scale, while Bennett is also developing a Netflix animated comedy called Dealies.
body: Common Side Effects was an unexpected treat when it premiered in February 2025. Featuring trippy animation and the voice of Hank Hill himself (Mike Judge), the series follows a schlubby fungus expert named Marshall Cuso (Dave King) who discovers a rare species of "Blue Angel" mushroom that can seemingly cure any disease or physical injury. Marshall's discovery sets off a conspiracy thriller as both the federal government and the pharmaceutical industry race to find Marshall and take control of this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

The Adult Swim series was also a redemption of sorts for co-creator Joe Bennett, after his previous project, Scavengers Reign, was canceled by HBO Max, offloaded to Netflix, and then shelved again. So it comes as a relief that Bennett's Common Side Effects, which he co-created with Steve Hely (Veep), is getting a second season.

At a New York Comic Con 2026 panel, Bennett and Hely announced that Common Side Effects season 2 will debut Sunday, Jan. 24 at 11:00 p.m. ET on Adult Swim (and streaming the next day on HBO Max). Ahead of the announcement, Polygon was able to watch the first episode of season 2 and ask its creators a few questions about where the show is headed next.
Check out our conversation below, along with a few updates on Bennett's other animated projects.
There are light spoilers for Common Side Effects season 2 episode 1 in this article.
Polygon: Common Side Effects season 2 introduces a new villain who seems to be hunting for the Blue Angel mushrooms. Can you tell me any more about this character?
Steve Hely: The character's name is Thomas, and there will be some backstory that'll unfold over the course of the season.
Joe Bennett: He's voiced by Bob Stephenson, who played Sam in Scavengers Reign.

Steve Hely: Our idea — without giving too much away — is that he came to the mushroom in his own way, and he's formed a kind of a religious obsession with it. When he learns that other people have it and are using it, he becomes obsessed with stopping them.

Joe Bennett: Similar to how we try to treat any of the villains in our show, we want to give him as much dimension as possible. You empathize with elements of Thomas. You kind of understand where he's coming from.
That's interesting, because he's not very sympathetic in the first episode. He's more like the Terminator.
Joe Bennett: Yeah, he's like an Anton Sugar.
Steve Hely: We always try to make sure there's a way to see it from their point of view. We'll get to that in the course of the season.
Season 2 also seems to be exploring the idea that people who use the Blue Angel mushroom can have shared hallucinations. Where is that plotline headed?

Joe Bennett: That is going to be an ongoing thread that'll sort of run parallel with the reality world throughout the season. Obviously, this new character is kind of familiar with that and you're going to do a lot of interweaving. For Marshall, the deeper he's getting, he's unpacking a lot of stuff that he didn't know was possible.
Steve Hely: And maybe getting a little scared of it.
Joe Bennett: It's a Pandora's Box kind of a thing.

Steve Hely: There is a side effect to this thing, and the limits of it are not quite understood. The idea that everybody who takes this mushroom is connected in this other realm opens up a lot of possibilities and creates some fun opportunities for very cool animation.
How has the animation evolved in season 2?

Steve Hely: This is a very ambitious season. They're going to a lot of different locations. There's a higher shot count, which is always a little bit of a burden on the team. There's a lot more in the Portal World that is bigger scale overall.

Joe Bennett: After season 1, we can now flex in these other areas and geek out on it. There's more rough animation that we were able to do. There's more stuff that we're able to do in-house and take bigger swings on with these action scenes.
Season 1 had some really interesting things to say about both the good and evil sides of the pharmaceutical industry. Where does that go in season 2?

Steve Hely: Our characters confront some of the challenges of making something safe and getting it distributed. They start to realize that the people they think of as their enemies might have evolved that way for perfectly practical and sensible reasons. That's part of the theme of the show: You might hate the current system, but setting up a different one is very challenging.
Mike Judge played a pretty big part in season 1 as the pharmaceutical executive, Rick. He also executive produces the show. How involved is he in season 2?
Steve Hely: He reads everything, and he's awesome to bounce stuff off of.
Joe Bennett: Rick's got a pretty big role in season 2. He's actually one of my favorite characters in this season.
Before I go, I need to ask about Scavengers Reign. Is there any chance we'll ever get a second season of that show or is it dead?
Joe Bennett: TBD. There's a huge fan base. But I don't know. We'll see.
Steve Hely: You're gonna be in the nursing home, saying, "We're working on it! One day!" [laughs]
Joe, you've also got a new animated show coming out on Netflix called Dealies. Where does that sit in your body of work?

Joe Bennett: My earlier original shorts are more sort of like comedy-based and comedy-focused. I think it's kind of pulling a lot more from that sort of thing. It's an episodic comedy series where a bunch of current characters work together in a big box store.
Steve Hely: Well, it's very Joe Bennett in that it's very character-based. Very observed. Kind of an offbeat kind of character. Exists in our real world, but capturing weirdness.
Joe Bennett: It's a big box store versus mom-and-pop brick-and-mortars. There's an antique store across the street that is really struggling to stay in business. So it's sort of playing with that."
How many seasons of Common Side Effects would you like to make in total?
Steve Hely: We want to tell 40 to 100 seasons. We see it as this constantly unfolding novel with many chapters that can expand in different directions and come back around.

articles.headline: Panama struck by 2 powerful earthquakes, U.S. Geological Survey says
keyFacts: Two earthquakes measuring magnitude 7.7 and 6.6 struck Panama on Friday, prompting evacuations and aftershocks, the USGS said.
Several injuries and structural damage were reported in central provinces, though the Panama Canal maintained normal operations, officials said.
Specialized technical teams are inspecting Panama Canal facilities for possible damage, the Panama Canal Authority said.
body: A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Panama's southern tip on Friday morning, shaking buildings more than 100 miles away in the capital and prompting evacuations, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. A second powerful 6.6 magnitude earthquake struck the country later in the day following a series of aftershocks.

The initial quake was centered about 7 miles southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba and struck at a depth of about 7 miles, the USGS said. The 6.6 magnitude quake came about two and a half hours later, with its epicenter about 8 miles west of Río Grande on Panama's Pacific coast and a depth of about 6 miles.
Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino said authorities had not documented anyone killed or injured as of Friday evening, though he cautioned that could change in the coming hours or days.
"Nobody was ready, and no one is ever ready for this type of disaster," Mulino said.
The U.S. Pacific Tsunami Warning Center had initially warned about the possibility of tsunami waves hitting Panama's coast, but later said the threat had passed.
Tremors were felt in Panama City, where buildings shook and people evacuated into the streets. Visibly shaken residents gathered outside as they waited for news.

"We felt it very strongly. It knocked things over in the kitchen, but we're OK, though we're very scared," Rosendo Domínguez, 60, who is from Herrera province, where the earthquake struck, told The Associated Press by phone. "Everyone is outside, scared."

Multiple aftershocks continued to rattle Panama, including several measuring magnitude 5.8, 5.5 and 5.2. Seismologists at the University of Panama recorded more than 45 aftershocks, though many were too weak to be felt.
Images of crumbling buildings and deep fissures slicing through roads added to fears across a region battered by a series of devastating earthquakes in recent months.

Two back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes roiled 's La Guaira state in June, killing more than 6,500 people and leaving 17,000 homeless. In August, a 7.4 magnitude earthquake in killed at least 289 people.
Mulino called for calm earlier Friday, writing on social media: "What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder."

Omar Smith of the National Civil Protection Service said on the Telemetro Reporta news channel that damage was concentrated in the central provinces of Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos. He said there were no reports of damage in the capital, which is known for its hundreds of skyscrapers.

Smith said several injuries have been reported, including one person struck by debris from a partially collapsed structure in the city of Penonomé, around 93 miles from the capital. He confirmed a partial collapse and cracks at the cathedral in the district's main square, as well as damage in the governor's office building and the Dos Continentes hotel.

Local news outlets also reported that the Church of San Atanasio, a colonial-style Catholic church in Panama's Los Santos province, had collapsed. The church was declared a National Historic Heritage Site in 1938. Elsewhere, including in Veraguas province, large fissures ran along roadways.

Tocumen International Airport in Panama City, one of the region's busiest airports with more than 20 million passengers in 2025, temporarily suspended operations after the first quake but said Friday afternoon that it was reopening.

The Panama Canal Authority said operations were continuing normally along the key global trade route. It said its priority was the safety of employees, vessels and crews and that specialized technical teams were inspecting facilities for possible damage.

The last major earthquake to cause widespread damage in Panama struck in 1991. A magnitude 7.4 quake centered in nearby Costa Rica killed 23 people, injured 559, and left thousands of people homeless in the border Bocas del Toro region.
Earthquakes are common, especially along Panama's border with Costa Rica and its Pacific coast, because of the interaction of several tectonic plates, including Cocos, Nazca and Caribbean plates.
Panama lies along the "Ring of Fire," a 25,000-mile arc of volcanoes and fault lines around the Pacific Basin, where most of the world's earthquakes occur.

Nearby countries sent messages of support Friday afternoon. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella expressed his solidarity with the Panamanian people and their government during what he called "difficult times."
"Panama is not alone! You can count on Colombia's support and our full willingness to provide whatever assistance is needed," he wrote on social media.
The U.S. Embassy in Panama said it was "closely monitoring" the aftermath of the quake and accounting for the welfare of its citizens in Panama, a well-known retirement destination for Americans.

articles.headline: 'Overcooked broke you apart and Stage Fright is there to put you back together'
keyFacts: Ghost Town Games is developing a new co-op adventure game called Stage Fright, which is published by Hello Games.
Developers said Stage Fright focuses on positive communication and building relationships, unlike their previous game, Overcooked.
In Stage Fright, two players guide kids through puzzles using physical items and split-screen play online or locally.
body: I introduced Overcooked to two of my friends one day back in 2016. One day being the key phrase here. The Overcooked games are on our list of the best co-op games, but the series has a reputation for ruining relationships—in China it's apparently known as "The Divorce Kitchen". I don't recall actually fighting with my friends, but the tension was thick enough that we quickly went back to playing Jackbox instead.

That makes Stage Fright, which is being published by No Man's Sky developer Hello Games, kind of an interesting pivot for Ghost Town Games. It's the next co-op adventure from the makers of Overcooked, but it's aimed at building relationships with your play partner instead of leaving you irked at them.
Here's what Stage Fright's developers have to say about the tonal shift a decade later.
"Overcooked broke you apart and Stage Fright is there to put you back together," said co-director Oliver De-Vine, when we spoke over Zoom in September.

"I think there's a sense of us trying to be constructive with co-op, and trying to be a constructive and positive force in the world," De-Vine said. "Not that there's anything negative, necessarily, about having a fun argument with your friends! But we're trying to foster community in our games. [They're] about communication between people, and less about being very good with the fidelity of a controller."

"It's exciting to us, the idea that the people who are good at our games are the ones who are good at communicating," said games designer Phil Duncan. "Certainly with Overcooked, one of the things we found with [demoing it at] conventions is that you would find a bunch of teenage boys would come and play it, and play in complete silence, and they'd fail the level horribly.

"And then you'd get two people, we had a little girl come up, and she was like eight years old, playing with her friend, and they're chatting the whole time. And they smashed through it, and they played absolutely effortlessly."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
Couch co-op, even without a couch
To make the co-op vibe of Stage Fright even more chummy, Ghost Town Games wants its players to feel like they're sitting on the couch with their friend—even when they're playing over the internet.

"I think it's a unique experience, local co-op particularly, versus playing games online," De-Vine said. "Even though our game is both local and online, we are trying to make the experience of online as similar to the local experience as possible. So the game is splitscreen online as well, because it does depend on being able to see what the other player is doing and communicate about what they're seeing in the environment."
"The ideal situation is that you're sat next to someone and you're nudging them and you point at the same thing. So it's as close as we can get to that online," Duncan said.

In Stage Fright, two players will guide a pair of kids through a Luigi's Mansion-style adventure where they'll have to tackle puzzles, avoid threats, and solve a mystery, with nothing to rely on but their partners. While there's more complexity in the adventure than in their chaotic kitchens, the devs didn't want to lose the accessibility of Overcooked's single-button action.
"Imagine family-friendly Silent Hill"
"When we talk about puzzle aspects or escape room aspects, we're trying to avoid having a game where you have to get a notepad out and write things down," De-Vine said.

"Everything is communicated between the players verbally. It's got adventure game elements, but without an inventory. There's no inventory management. Everything is physical items you're carrying around in a similar way to Overcooked, sort of quite large, obvious, chunky items, and that is again trying to make sure that everything is out loud in communication."
I asked if it was a linear type of game, where players need to solve puzzles in order, or if they'll be able to try a different puzzle and come back later when they get stuck.

"Similar to how you would find an escape room experience, where you'll find a clue, and it won't necessarily be linked to the thing [you're solving], you'll have to remember that for later," De-Vine said.
"It's linear in the way that Silent Hill is linear. Which is a weird comparison because it's not much like it," he said, laughing. "But you know, imagine family-friendly Silent Hill."

Chris started playing PC games in the 1980s, started writing about them in the early 2000s, and (finally) started getting paid to write about them in the late 2000s. Following a few years as a regular freelancer, PC Gamer hired him in 2014, probably so he'd stop emailing them asking for more work. Chris has a love-hate relationship with survival games and an unhealthy fascination with the inner lives of NPCs. He's also a fan of offbeat simulation games, mods, and ignoring storylines in RPGs so he can make up his own.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy furious as Trump announces deal to buy Russian diesel
keyFacts: Donald Trump announced an agreement with Vladimir Putin to purchase Russian diesel fuel for the American and global markets.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the deal, saying it supports Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine.
Russia will immediately supply 300,000 tons of diesel fuel, followed by 500,000 tons in November, according to Trump.
body: Donald Trump was on a fresh collision course with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and European allies on Friday after a stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel, upending years of US and western pressure on the Kremlin to end its four-and-a-half year war against Ukraine.
Zelenskyy reacted furiously to Trump’s announcement of the deal with President Vladimir Putin of Russia, calling it “absolutely terrible” and “not fair and not honest”.

In a move likely to create a fresh crisis with Washington’s Nato allies, Trump announced the deal with Putin on his Truth Social network, saying it was essential to reduce fuel prices in the US, which have soared as a result of his decision to go to war with Iran.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter,” Trump wrote.
“Based on the condition of their diesel refineries, Russia will then deliver, within a short period of time, 3,000,000 tons of diesel fuel.”

He added: “Diesel prices for Americans and, indeed, the world, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST! Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my greatest priority.”

Fuel prices have rocketed due to Iran’s closure of the strait of Hormuz, a strategically sensitive choke point that was the passageway for 20% of the global oil supplies before the war. While costs have risen for motorists – with a gallon of fuel now averaging $4.20 – it is the soaring price of diesel, which last month rose to a record high of $6.52, that has inflicted the most political damage to Trump and the Republicans as November’s midterm approach.
Diesel is the main supply chain fuel, and a rise in its costs feeds into consumer prices and also hurts US farmers, who need to operate machinery.

The agreement was criticized by Democrats, who said it undercut a law Trump signed last month allowing for a broad range of sanctions on Russian banks, officials and tankers, as well as directing him to impose steep tariffs on the top five importers of oil or natural gas from Russia. The law gave Trump wide discretion to make exception to its provisions.
But the fiercest response came from Zelenskyy, who told Axios that it “looks like a a happy birthday present for Putin. It looks absolutely terrible.” The Russian leader turned 74 earlier this week.

In a long social media post, Zelenskyy, who has had an uneasy relationship with Trump, said the deal amounted to an “an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged”. Russia was likely to repay it with “further terror and perfidy”.
“It plays into Russia’s hands – allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said.
Trump announced the oil deal as his envoys, Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner, met with Ukrainian and European officials in Miami to discuss proposals to end the war.

Zelenskyy, in a separate statement released by Ukraine’s embassy in Washington on Friday, said the Ukrainian negotiators had been “used as a smokescreen for the deal” which he called “a weak decision by strong partners”.
“That is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other.” he said.

Trump has recently criticized Ukraine for attacking Russian diesel refineries, calling on Zelenskyy to choose alternative targets. The Ukrainian leader rejected the request unless Russia accepted a reciprocal de-escalation plan that would stop Moscow attacking Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.

The agreement also comes on the heels of rising tensions between Russia and Washington’s Nato allies in Europe, amid speculation that Moscow might be preparing military action intended to test the alliance’s resolve.

The latest development is likely to lead to a further deterioration of Zelenskyy’s relationship with the Trump administration. He was infamously ambushed by Trump and the vice president, JD Vance, last year in an explosive White House encounter when the president told him: “You don’t have the cards.”
But Trump has since reportedly grown disenchanted with Putin, expressing disappointment in his failure to reach a deal.

Trump’s willingness to reach an agreement with Putin that will lower fuel costs comes despite Russia’s support for Iran in its war with the US. Russia is believed to have given Iran satellite intelligence and overhead surveillance data detailing the locations of American forces, ships, aircraft and military bases. It has also provided drone component and ammunition.

articles.headline: Trump not attending hyped Alabama-Georgia game as Hurricane Isaias barrels toward Gulf

body: Saturday’s SEC matchup between Alabama and Georgia will now be without President Donald Trump in the crowd.
Trump, who was expected to attend the game at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Ala., said Friday that he will not be going due to extreme weather threats from Hurricane Isaias.

“Based on the fact that a huge Hurricane/Storm is coming, it is important to have our wonderful First Responders, Law Enforcement, and others, focused on that Storm, and in no way be thinking about the safety, or presence, of the President of the United States, ME!” Trump wrote on Truth Social Friday afternoon.
Trump added that he plans to attend games for both teams later in the season.
“Therefore, I will miss that potentially unbelievable Game, Alabama vs. Georgia but, hopefully, the Game will go on despite the weather! I will be visiting both of those Teams at a later date.”
Hurricane Isaias, which is expected to make landfall along the Gulf Coast late Friday evening, poses a major threat to the Southeast, with Tuscaloosa near its expected path.
Precautions surrounding the game have already been taken, with ESPN’s “College GameDay” programming moving inside to Alabama’s basketball arena due to the weather.

Despite the hurricane — which is expected to strengthen to a Category 3 storm by the time it reaches the coast — Saturday’s game is still on as of Friday evening, with Alabama insisting that the school is looking at the weather.

“Alabama athletics continues to closely monitor the weather forecast ahead of Saturday’s football game, with the safety and well-being of the student-athletes, coaches, staff and fans as our highest priority,” the university said in a statement Wednesday night.
“We remain in close communication with the National Weather Service, the Southeastern Conference office and the University of Georgia as we observe conditions.

articles.headline: Let’s All Be Happy This AAA Minesweeper Game Isn’t Real
keyFacts: Writer and programmer Mike Lacher created a playable browser parody called Triple-A Minesweeper.
The parody resembles standard Minesweeper but features a main character who receives phone calls from various fictional characters.
Players can complete the game to trigger a predictable twist ending.
body: Minesweeper has been around for decades and it's probably overdue for some modern flourishes. Now there's a Triple-A Minesweeper parody that offers a hilarious look at what a Minesweeper update might look like.

The Triple-A Minesweeper was created by writer and programmer Mike Lacher, and it's fully playable as a browser game on his site . Aside from the intentionally pretentious title cards touting the involvement of Unreal Engine, Nvidia, Bink Video, and Wwise, Triple A Minesweeper looks and plays almost exactly like the regular Minesweeper.

However, the best way to enjoy this parody is by simply not doing anything at all. The main character, "Sweeper," will sit around and repeat things like, "I gotta sweep these mines," while receiving calls from newly created characters in the game. Lacher seems to have taken his inspiration from Grand Theft Auto 5, Metal Gear Solid, and even Cyberpunk 2077.

Among the callers are Nora, a potential love interest for Sweeper. Additionally, an underworld figure called The Don repeatedly calls for Sweeper to head down to his club while hinting at the latter's sinister past in Singapore. Meanwhile, the chipper DJ Dan celebrates Sweeper's efforts on behalf of New Dawn City.

In another amusing touch, Sweeper never acknowledges any of the other characters and keeps repeating the same lines over and over. It is possible to complete the game, which triggers a twist ending that probably wasn't that difficult to predict.
Although Lacher leaves the parody on that note, it would have been even funnier if the game's coda mentioned that Triple-A Minesweeper flopped and cost Microsoft hundreds of millions of dollars.

Microsoft hasn't done too much with Minesweeper in the past few years, although it was added to Microsoft Teams as a playable game. The company has also previously created a Minesweeper-themed ugly Christmas sweater .

body: Mike Flanagan is a busy man. Just this week, his TV series remake of Stephen King‘s horror classic, Carrie, premiered on Prime Video. Clayface, the body-horror movie inspired by the DC Comics character, for which he cowrote the script, hits theaters on Oct. 23.
Now, he’s onto promoting his next completed project, The Exorcist: Martyrs, a film he called “the scariest movie I’ve ever made,” while at Friday’s Blumhouse panel at New York Comic Con.

If you’ve been keeping track, Flanagan’s name has been attached to the iconic horror franchise, which began in 1973 and is based on the William Peter Blatty novel of the same name. Since Linda Blair terrified audiences as the demon-possessed young girl, Regan MacNeil, the movie series expanded. There have been sequels, a prequel and even a short-lived TV show.
More from CNET
In 2023, David Gordon Green attempted to reboot the franchise with The Exorcist: The Believer. Now, it’s Flanagan’s turn.

The Exorcist: Martyrs gives a new spin on the Exorcist canon and injects a Minderhunter-style serial killer narrative element into the mix. If you watched the TV series I mentioned above, you’ll notice a similar procedural vibe in the brand-new trailer that dropped during the panel. And if you’re an Exorcist III stan, I’m sure you’ll be happy with the just released clip, as it’s got that similar brooding feeling here.

The Exorcist: Martyrs stars Scarlett Johansson as an NYPD detective tracking a serial killer named Father Sunday (John Leguizamo), who uses Catholic iconography in his kills. Chiwetel Ejiofor, fresh out of The Backrooms, also stars in the film, opposite Laurence Fishburne, Sasha Calle and Jacobi Jupe.

If you’ve been yearning for the Mike Flanagan era of Oculus and The Haunting of Hill House, The Exorcist: Martyrs feels like the filmmaker is back in his terrifying groove. While I’m still waiting for his adaptation of Stephen King’s The Dark Tower to see the light of day, this will have to do.
The Exorcist: Martyrs premieres in theaters on Friday, March 12, 2027.

articles.headline: Trump’s press secretary pick Katie Zacharia comes from Noem-Lewandowski era at DHS
keyFacts: President Donald Trump has selected former Department of Homeland Security official Katie Zacharia as White House press secretary.
Zacharia previously worked for several weeks as deputy spokeswoman at the Department of Homeland Security before abruptly leaving her post.

body: President Donald Trump has tapped former Department of Homeland Security public affairs official Katie Zacharia as White House press secretary , a choice that caught current and former DHS officials who had worked with Zacharia off guard.

Zacharia, 41, worked for several weeks earlier this year as deputy spokeswoman for the 270,000-person federal department before abruptly leaving her post around the time then-Secretary Kristi Noem and special government employee Corey Lewandowski left.

One DHS official who worked with Zacharia during her stint wrote in a text message to the Washington Examiner that she was “full on MAGA” but “she didn’t know DHS enough to be an effective (or accurate) communicator.”
“Seems [too] timid to live up to the challenges of the job but I wish her the best of the luck,” the DHS official said.
The Daily Mail reported in March that Zacharia was brought in by Lewandowski in mid-February and “quit” in late March “amid fears she would be fired due to her alliance with” Lewandowksi.

Shortly after her departure, the White House pushed Noem and Lewandowski out of the department amid scandals connected to the department’s purchases of a luxury airplane, advertising, and immigrant detention contracts.

Zacharia’s background is as a conservative attorney, former attorney for the World Bank in China, and Republican political campaigns. She stepped on as deputy assistant secretary for public affairs at DHS following the abrupt departure of assistant secretary for public affairs, Tricia McLaughlin. She was hired to be the “on-camera face of Trump’s immigration crackdown,” according to the Daily Mail .
Zacharia has branded herself as a Fox News commentator, which is a paid position, and has the position listed on her LinkedIn profile as of Friday.
WHO IS KATIE ZACHARIA, TRUMP’S NEXT WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY?
Fox News told the Daily Mail in March that Zacharia was not a commentator for the network, but that she had appeared as a guest.
The White House did not respond to a request for clarification about Zacharia’s Fox News claim.

articles.headline: Trump names new press secretary to succeed Karoline Leavitt
keyFacts: Donald Trump announced that Katie Zacharia will serve as the next White House press secretary, succeeding Karoline Leavitt.
Zacharia previously worked as a senior communications advisor to Truth Social and at the Department of Homeland Security.
Leavitt will begin providing commentary for Fox News starting on November 1 after stepping down to spend time with family.
body: US President Donald Trump on Friday announced that Katie Zacharia will be the next White House press secretary, succeeding Karoline Leavitt.
Zacharia is a 'loyal and brilliant supporter,' Trump says

In a post on his Truth Social network, Trump said it was a "great honor" to appoint Zacharia to the role, calling her a "loyal and brilliant supporter" and member of the Make America Great Again movement.

Zacharia, a 42-year-old native of California, had been serving as Senior Communications Advisor to Truth Social. She had also earlier worked as Deputy Assistant Secretary for Public Affairs at the Department of Homeland Security.
Zacharia, in a post on X, thanked Trump and said "his leadership is a blessing to this country."

"The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our country and communicating to the American people the major wins that the administration is making every single day," Zacharia said. "I look forward to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out."
Zacharia said her predecessor Leavitt was "fabulous" and that she set a "high standard" to meet for the press secretary job.
Will Zacharia follow Leavitt's combative approach?
Trump had announced that Leavitt would resign in August to spend more time with her young children and family.
Earlier this week, conservative-leaning broadcaster Fox News announced that Leavitt would provide commentary on the network starting from November 1.
Leavitt took a combative approach to questions from the White House press corps during her tenure as press secretary.

In January, she called a White House reporter a "left-wing hack" after a question regarding the fatal US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) shooting of American citizen Renee Good in Minneapolis. She also had to defend Trump's controversial handling of the Epstein files and the ongoing Iran war.

Leavitt managed to stay in the role for over 18 months — a long tenure for a high-stress job under a demanding president. During Trump's first term from 2017 to 2021, he had four press secretaries: Sean Spicer, Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Stephanie Grisham and Kayleigh McEnany.

Zacharia's tenure comes as Trump faces low approval ratings due to high energy prices amid the Iran war and the looming midterms on November 3, where the opposition Democrats are expected to make major congressional gains.

articles.headline: Man City whistleblower to remain in witness protection
keyFacts: Portuguese authorities suspended a decision to end witness protection for Football Leaks founder Rui Pinto, allowing him to remain in protection.
Pinto disclosed confidential financial documents that helped trigger a Premier League investigation into Manchester City.
Pinto will now have 10 days to assess a risk assessment indicating a low threat to his safety.
body: - Published

The Portuguese computer hacker who released documents which helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City will remain in witness protection after authorities in the country suspended the decision to end it.
Football Leaks founder Rui Pinto had been scheduled to leave the protection programme on Saturday, a ruling he previously said had put him in a "life-threatening situation".
Pinto, 37, disclosed a tranche of confidential football documents, including emails and financial records relating to the English Premier League side.
In 2018, he shared documents with German magazine Der Spiegel, which used them for investigations into City's finances and alleged breaches of financial fair play rules.
City were recently found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. They have appealed against the decision.
Pinto became part of Portugal's witness protection programme in 2020 after agreeing to co-operate with authorities and provide information obtained through the Football Leaks operation.

However, in a statement on Friday,, external Portugal's Ministry of Justice said a decision to remove Pinto from witness protection had been reversed for the time being, with the body responsible for it - the special security programmes commission - having not adequately "notified" Pinto of grounds for its termination or given him the opportunity to challenge the decision.
Pinto will now be given 10 days to assess a risk assessment conducted by the special security programmes commission that indicates a low threat to his safety.

He posted on X, external thanking Portugal's Minister of Justice, Rita Alarcao Judice and saying the commission's initial decision had clearly violated the law and amounted to a "manifest abuse of power".
Pinto has described himself as a whistleblower, but was convicted in Portugal of offences including illegal access to data and attempted extortion and given a four-year suspended sentence.
He wore a bulletproof vest during his first trial in 2020, which was also subject to heightened security measures.
Earlier this year, he was acquitted of 241 counts of illegally accessing email accounts belonging to a number of sports bodies in Portugal, including Benfica.

articles.headline: Konami Planning 'Second and Third Waves' of New Silent Hill Games
keyFacts: Konami is planning second and third waves of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto.
Okamoto stated that the first wave of titles was released successfully and received high praise from players and critics.
Okamoto did not share specific details, but he noted that Konami is currently looking at a number of new projects.
body: Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto.

Okamoto offered a foggy glimpse into the classic horror franchise's future during an interview featured in Famitsu Issue 1965 (via Game Observer ). The series ended a long, painful drought without new games with an initial wave of new releases over the last few years, and now that this first batch is out, Konami is already looking forward to what it can do next.
"All three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully, so we’re relieved (laughs)," he noted. "They’ve also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it."

Okamoto continued: "Successfully launching this 'first wave' comes with great relief, but we’re not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves. We can’t share specific details, but we’re currently looking at a number of projects."

The first wave of Konami's return to Silent Hill – which included titles like the Silent Hill 2 remake , Silent Hill f , and last month's Silent Hill: Townfall – rolled out throughout the last few years. Townfall arrived as the most recent installment when it dropped players into the shoes of protagonist Simon Ordell in a '90s Scotland just last month.

It received generally favorable reviews, with IGN giving it an 8/10 . We said, "Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm."

It's a successful run of games that Konami is happy with, but getting here wasn't easy. After Hideo Kojima's Silent Hills failed to materialize, Okamoto said he had a hard time convincing higher-ups that more games was the way to go. However, as far as he was concerned, "just one remake is not enough," adding, "as a producer, I cannot let it end only with that."
"If there were only one release, wouldn’t people think that the development is going to be cancelled again, I thought," Okamoto added.

While Konami's plan to launch additional waves of Silent Hill games spells a promising future for fans who have missed the franchise, we have known that the series would continue in some form. Bloober Team, the horror-centric developer responsible for the Silent Hill 2 remake, confirmed it was working on a remake of the original Silent Hill last year.

articles.headline: The Trump administration plans a public killing
keyFacts: The Pentagon announced plans to publicly execute and livestream the death of former Army major Nidal Hasan via firing squad.
Hasan was sentenced to death for a 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood that killed 13 people and wounded over 30.
The execution is scheduled for December 3, but Hasan's legal team could potentially delay it through federal court challenges.
body: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth speaks from a stage in Sparrows Point, Maryland, on October 6, 2026. | Win McNamee/Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: The Trump administration is planning a public killing.

What’s happening? On Thursday, the Pentagon announced that it would execute Nidal Hasan, a former Army major sentenced to death for a 2009 mass shooting on a military base, publicly and on livestream.

The execution, if it happens, would be unprecedented: The last widely reported public execution in the US was 90 years ago , in Kentucky, but to stream a death live would be something else entirely. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has promoted the announcement with something approaching glee, telling a reporter that “we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it.”
What’s the context? According to the Pentagon, Hasan will be executed via firing squad on December 3 — the first such execution by the military in more than 80 years.

Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, was sentenced to death in 2013 by a military jury following a court-martial for the 2009 shooting, when he killed 13 people and wounded more than 30 at Fort Hood in Texas. The execution is set to be carried out at the same Army post.

Will the Pentagon go through with this? It’s unclear, for multiple reasons. The Pentagon’s announcement that Hasan’s death will be livestreamed has generated a great deal of bipartisan pushback, as well as condemnation by religious groups , though that is unlikely to stop the execution itself.

The head of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops decried the decision to livestream the execution as “a barbaric promotion of a culture of death,” and retiring Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC) called it the decision “beyond disgusting.”
“Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do,” Tillis wrote in a post on X.
On Friday, Vice President JD Vance also said that he was unsure if the livestream would take place .
Hasan’s legal team could also delay the execution substantially — potentially for multiple years — by challenging his detention in federal court, though he has exhausted the military appeals process.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

The driest (non-polar) desert in the world, the Atacama in South America, was in full bloom late last month after record-setting rainfall. You can read more about the science behind the wildflowers here , or just enjoy some spectacular photos here (it’s a gift link). Either way, I hope it brings you some joy.

articles.headline: Neanderthal wooden tools from Spain found preserved in stone
keyFacts: Spanish archaeologists cataloged 597 Neanderthal wooden tool impressions preserved in stone at the Abric Romaní rock shelter.
The preserved artifacts include spears, digging sticks, bark trays, shelter components, and a novel wooden club.
Archaeologist M. Gema Chacón said the discoveries show Neanderthals routinely engaged in woodworking for varied subsistence tasks beyond hunting.
body: The Stone Age owes its name to tools that survived to our time. The material early humans worked with most, though, was probably wood because it is so much easier to process. Unfortunately, we know very little about Paleolithic woodwork because wood rots relatively quickly. But at Abric Romaní, a rock shelter in Capellades, west of Barcelona, mineral-rich water coated wooden Neanderthal tools in a limestone-like crust. When wood rotted away, it left behind hollow molds that faithfully reflect its shape.

In a recent Science Advances study, a team of Spanish archaeologists has cataloged 597 wooden remains from Neanderthal living areas dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago. They found spears, digging sticks, bark trays, parts of shelters, and a club unlike anything seen before, suggesting Neanderthals were likely much more than just Homo sapiens’ dumber cousins.
Beyond hunting gear

The oldest wooden artifacts we have are mostly weapons. They include spears from a German town called Schöningen, a spear tip from Clacton-on-Sea in England, and the spear found alongside an elephant skeleton in Lehringen, Germany. Most came from waterlogged sediments, where a lack of oxygen slowed decay.

The spears mostly give us information about how Neanderthals hunted. The findings at Abric Romaní are different because the finds come from a place where Neanderthals lived, slept, cooked, and made tools over the course of some 20,000 years.

“We have a sample of wooden tools for different subsistence activities, not only hunting,” says M. Gema Chacón, an archaeologist at the Catalan Institute of Human Paleoecology and Social Evolution (IPHES-CERCA) and co-author of the study. Because wood turns up in level after level, it shows that woodworking was routine for Neanderthals rather than an occasional one-off.

articles.headline: Google teases its new 'Fitbit Edge' wearable ahead of an October 12 reveal
keyFacts: Google teased a new fitness tracker called the Fitbit Edge through social media posts on Instagram and X.
Dealabs reported that the device will cost around €179 and fit between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5.
Google plans to officially reveal the new wearable on October 12.
body: Google teases its new 'Fitbit Edge' wearable ahead of an October 12 reveal
The company has essentially confirmed it's releasing another fitness tracker.

Previous leaked images revealed the name and design of Google's rumored "Fitbit Edge" fitness tracker and now the company has essentially confirmed both in new posts on Instagram and X. The wearable is rumored to fit between the screenless Fitbit Air Google launched earlier this year and the more premium Pixel Watch 5.

Google's posts include an image of what appears to be a side button on the new wearable, and the following caption: "Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.26." The choice to capitalize "Edge" seems to confirm the name of the wearable, and October 12 is likely the day Google plans to reveal it.
Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.26 pic.twitter.com/1zRU0eoAS7
— Google Health (@googlehealth) October 9, 2026

Images of this new Fitbit device have been kicking around since at least August, when 9to5Google spotted an unnamed fitness tracker in some of Google's Pixel 11 marketing. But the name of the wearable wasn't revealed until Android Headlines shared images of the Fitbit Edge and details of its built-in apps and health tracking features earlier this week. Those details were further fleshed out in a report from French magazine Dealabs, which confirmed the device's design and name, and included additional information on its battery life and possible price. The Edge will reportedly last for up to seven days on a charge if its always-on display is disabled, and two days if it's on, and could cost €179 (about $200) when it goes on sale in Europe. But considering the Fitbit Air starts at $99 in the US and €99 in Europe, the new tracker could wind up being closer to $180 in the US.

The last similarly-sized fitness tracker Google introduced was the Fitbit Charge 6 in 2023, so the company is due for a new release. If it's everything reporting has described it to be, the Fitbit Edge seems like a natural step up from the Fitbit Air, and another way to push people to a Google Health Premium subscription. We'll just have to wait until October 12 to see if Google follows through.

articles.headline: Kalshi probes shady bets on new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia: report

body: Kalshi is probing a series of shady bets about the new White House press secretary, according to a report published hours after Katie Zacharia was named to the high-profile job.
The massive prediction market platform said it was looking into wagers that accurately predicted the conservative commentator would land the role, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
A minimum of three small but precisely-timed bets were reportedly placed on Zacharia not long before news outlets began reporting the news, netting the bettors a few thousand bucks.
The Journal scoured publicly available Kalshi data to find a $19 bet placed around 10:43 p.m. Thursday. That stood to net the bettor $1,896.
Two more bets reportedly came around 1:41 p.m. Friday, the paper reported. The wagers of $74 and $80 were poised to bring in $7,712 total.
A Kalshi spokeswoman declined to talk about the bets on the White House press secretary, telling The Post, “We can’t comment on ongoing investigations.”
Recent months have seen a number of shady trades on Kalshi and rival Polymarket — which are facing a mountain of litigation from state authorities.

A US special forces soldier was charged in the spring for allegedly using classified information about the mission to capture Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro to win more than $400,000 on the Polymarket.

More recently, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission reportedly launched a probe of unusual trading activity on Kalshi after billions of dollars worth of near-identical crypto trades raised questions about possible “wash trading.”

articles.headline: Long live the mechanical keyboard
keyFacts: Keychron has produced dozens of mechanical keyboards, keypads, and mice since launching via Kickstarter in 2017.
Keychron mechanical keyboards offer swappable key caps, Bluetooth connectivity, and retro designs.
Keychron keyboard prices range from $60 to $200, while its gaming keypad is currently sold out.
body: For a writer, the mechanical keyboard is a beautiful thing. It’s certainly not necessary for everyone, but a well-designed mechanical keyboard can turn a tedious day of typing into an aesthetically pleasing experience.

Given that most of my days involve sitting at a desk for hours, having a keyboard that I enjoy using is a necessity. I first got a mechanical keyboard about two years ago — the Keychron K2 — and I’ve never looked back.

Keychron is one of the most prominent brands within the mechanical keyboard industry, having made a name for itself after initially launching via Kickstarter back in 2017. The company has since produced dozens of different keyboards (as well as keypads) and a variety of mouse models.

Unlike other electronics, there isn’t a whole lot to owning a mechanical keyboard. The simplicity is part of the appeal. You unbox them, set them up (the K2 comes with little tilt legs that give you a slightly better angle from which to type), and plug them in.

From here, you have a couple of different options. The K2 comes with a simple USB cable, but there’s also an option for Bluetooth connection. If you value a clean, minimalist workspace, Bluetooth is probably the way to go.

While I am loyal to my older Keychron K2, there are a few upgraded and newer versions to consider. Keychron has released a variety of new models over the past two years, with a broad range of features and price tags.

In many cases, the form factor is the draw. One of the more interesting releases, called the Keychron K8 HE Wireless Magnetic Switch Custom Keyboard, comes with an all-wood body and is equipped with an LED backlight. That one is substantially more expensive at around $200. The K2, meanwhile, costs $60. But if you’re into the look, maybe it’s worth it.

If you’re a gamer, there’s also Keychron’s C0 HE One-Handed 8K Keyboard, which is a keypad built for convenience and speed and has an industrial aesthetic to it. However, interested gamers will have to wait — as it’s currently sold out.
The company has also updated its K, Q, and V series keyboards, with many of those ranging in price from $100 to $200, depending on the features and model.

One of the appealing elements of owning a mechanical keyboard is the versatility. You can swap out the key caps for a wide variety of others (indeed, there’s a whole submarket devoted to this) or make your own custom caps (I’ve never gone that overboard).

There is also the sound, of course. Some people balk at the accentuated noise of loudly clacking keys, but I’m a fan. In fact, the sound is one of the key selling points for a lot of consumers. The distinct auditory experience produced by said keyboards has even made its way into ASMR videos.

For me, the Keychron’s biggest selling point is its retro form factor. I get really nostalgic for old school electronics, and Keychron scratches this itch pretty well. It’s a beautiful-looking device, which brings to mind a different era of computing, when the style was more workman-like, less minimalist.
As far as home office purchases go, you could do a lot worse than to pick yourself up a piece of hardware that makes your desk look like it just time-traveled from the 1990s.

body: Empathetic Prototypes is one of the several new quests to complete in ARC Raiders and you can get it from Lance after completing the Someone Else’s Shoes. You’ll need to complete all the tasks and bring back something valuable to Lance to complete the objective.

Reach the Trench Towers in the Spaceport Trench

Screenshot and remix by Destructoid For the first task, head to the Trench Towers in the northern part of the Spaceport. articles.headline: Tottenham happy to be called name again after previous request to the media
keyFacts: Tottenham Hotspur is reincorporating 'Tottenham' into its club branding two years after asking media to avoid using the standalone name.
The club previously instructed media in a brand playbook to never refer to them simply as 'Tottenham'.
Tottenham sits bottom of the Premier League table with two points ahead of their upcoming match against Manchester United.
body: Tottenham have backtracked on their omission of ‘Tottenham’ from club branding – two years after requesting alternative names.
The north London club launched a new ‘brand identity’ in November 2024 that featured changes to their logo and signature font.
Spurs look as though they are heading back to being simply named as ‘Tottenham’ despite a past media request Getty
It was later revealed that they wrote to broadcasters asking for them to be referred to as either ‘Tottenham Hotspur’ or ‘Spurs’.
‘Tottenham’ was seemingly brushed aside but, as per The Athletic, it could be on its way back .
Fans attending home matches are said to have seen signs that read ‘This is Tottenham ‘ upon arrival.
They also launched a short film during the summer called ‘Tottenham ‘Til I Die’, with ‘Hotspur’ being dropped once again.
At the time of writing, the Premier League still call them ‘Tottenham Hotspur’ on their website, although this could change soon.
What did Tottenham want to be called?
The reintegration of ‘Tottenham’ comes after the new brand identity included a club request for what they wanted to be named as.
“When referring to the team or the brand, please use ‘Tottenham Hotspur’, ‘Tottenham Hotspur Football Club’ or ‘THFC’,” said a ‘Brand Playbook’.
It addd: “Never refer to our Club as ‘Tottenham’, ‘Tottenham Hotspur FC’ or ‘TH’.”
Founded in 1882, they were originally named ‘Hotspur Football Club’ and based in Northumberland Park, which is in north Tottenham.
‘Tottenham Hotspur Football Club’ became their official name two years later.
‘Tottenham Hotspur’ was the preferred name used by the club, although it looks as though it will be toned down Getty
Spurs are back!
After the three-week international break, Spurs return to Premier League action this weekend.
They travel to Manchester United on Saturday evening in search of their first win of the season.
Spurs lost 3-0 at Brentford on the opening weekend before falling to a 2-0 home defeat against Newcastle United.
Back-to-back 0-0 draws with Nottingham Forest and Everton were then followed by a 3-2 loss to Aston Villa.
The results mean they sit bottom of the Premier League table with two points gained from a possible 15.
As things stand, Spurs could be battling against relegation to the Championship yet again.

articles.headline: Decade-old RAM is making a comeback
keyFacts: Intel and AMD are producing new CPUs that support older DDR4 memory to address rising DDR5 RAM prices.
Gigabyte announced new motherboards for AMD's older AM4 platform alongside the relaunch of a Ryzen CPU.
New Intel chips compatible with DDR4 RAM are expected to launch in early 2027, according to Gigabyte.
body: CPU makers have noticed that the seemingly unending RAM price hikes are making it tough for a lot of us to upgrade our PCs. Their solution? A return to last-gen DDR4 RAM. Intel and AMD are making new CPUs that’ll support the older, more affordable type of memory.
Decade-old RAM is making a comeback
The RAM shortage is bringing back DDR4, with new Intel and AMD CPUs for older RAM, sockets, and chipsets.

On Friday, Gigabyte announced that two of its motherboard lines will support “upcoming” processors built on Intel’s LGA 1700 socket. That socket debuted in 2021 with the 12th gen Alder Lake CPUs and supported both DDR4 RAM and the then-new DDR5 RAM. Intel dropped it for a DDR5-only approach in 2024. But according to Gigabyte, the dual format support is now being revived, with new LGA 1700 chips “expected to launch in early 2027.”
Intel did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

This backtrack stems from LGA 1700’s cross-compatibility with both kinds of RAM — an advantage over its successor that’s recently become much more important. Intel’s strategy may be to offer users the choice of a new CPU that doesn’t require them to switch to new, and very expensive, DDR5 memory, too. AMD is doing something similar: in August, Gigabyte also announced a new series of motherboards for AMD’s last-gen, DDR4-compatible AM4 platform to go along with the 10th-anniversary relaunch of the Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU.

DDR4 started hitting the market in 2014 and has since been succeeded by the much faster DDR5. Under normal circumstances, buying new hardware to use technology that’s over a decade old would probably be a bad investment. But the RAM shortage is changing the math, with DDR4 RAM seemingly feeling the sting of price hikes much less than DDR5.

I recently saw the price disparity first-hand while shopping around for new RAM after a DDR4 kit abruptly died on me. Right now, a DDR5 32GB Corsair Vengeance RAM kit costs $620, while the corresponding DDR4 kit costs $260. Even though it’s more than 32GB of DDR4 RAM typically cost back in mid-2025, that’s more than double the price for DDR5! Of course, DDR5 has significant advantages, like higher speeds and better power efficiency. But those perks might not be worth the current price of admission.

It could be years before prices drop again, a reality that’s starting to really sink in with the official return of older sockets and chipsets. But at least it’s a good time to hang onto your DDR4 RAM.

articles.headline: We Might Be Cooked, As These Vibe-Coded Web Browser Ports Of Halo, The Simpsons: Hit And Run, And GTA: Vice City Seem To Work Perfectly
keyFacts: AI updates have enabled fast decompilation and creation of web browser ports for classic video games.
Reviewers found that several AI-decompiled browser ports of major games ran exceptionally well, with some even supporting online servers.
Publishers' legal teams are expected to face unprecedented challenges in addressing these unauthorized ports.
body: In the past couple of weeks, hundreds of vibe-coded, AI-decompiled emulators and games have appeared out of thin air. Why? Because Claudeâs latest update, Claude Opus 5.5, is extremely good at decompiling.

The short of it is that a gameâs source code can now be compiled and reconstructed in record timeâsomething that used to take coders months to achieve. All of those ânativeâ Fallout and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare ports and those AI-generated Super Mario 64 inside Elden Ring mash-up mods you may have seen are a direct result of this.

However, I think todayâs example is far and away the most concerning development so far, because Iâm forced to admit that these AI-decompiled web browser ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops, Halo: CE, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, Skate 3, and The Simpsons: Hit and Run actually seem to run very well.

Sure, lawyers for Take-Two and Microsoft and whoever else can send out some cease-and-desist letters and get these taken down. But then what? These browser ports were clearly easy and fast to create, so whatâs gonna stop people from just vibe-coding another version of these browser ports?
PLAY ALL THESE GAMES IN YOUR BROWSER
Your PC does not need the game installed!
you can play Black Ops zombies, Skate 3, Halo and MW2 and more GAMES all run in a browser tab now. full list in the comments.
School gaming is boutta be fire pic.twitter.com/sd98HQo8pf
— Radiant Optimizer (@RadiantOpti) October 8, 2026

This is IP protection whack-a-mole on a scale I donât think weâve seen since the advent of pirated DVDs. I genuinely donât know how you put the genie back in the bottle on something like this. And the worst part is, at least where the video game publishers will be concerned, some of these run perfectly.

I played through a bunch of the web browser ports of the games linked in the thread above, and some of them seemed to be borderline flawless. In the case of The Simpsons: Hit and Run, it might even be better than flawless, because I donât remember the game being able to target 240fps when I was a kid. Itâs also extremely worrying that one of the four different web browser ports of Halo: CE I played had working online serversâ¦and my ping was low.

Look, Iâm not happy about admitting this, but itâs the truthâand itâs a pretty straightforward one at that. Most of the games that are being ported to browsers are PS2- or PS3-era titles. You know how much RAM the PS3 had? About 512 megabytes. You know how much memory my web browser is currently using as I type this? About 1,200 megabytes.

Web browser ports havenât been limited by RAM usage for quite some timeâthe difference here is that Claude Opus 5.5 is an AI you can leave running overnight to decompile a game instead of painstakingly working your way through the code, like your grandpappy used to.
I donât know where we go from here. All I can say with any certainty is that video game publishersâ legal teams are going to be working overtime for the foreseeable future.
